title: How do you multiply big numbers in your head without losing the zeros?
description: Big numbers without losing the zeros: a quick way to do this case calculation in your head, with a worked example.
hook: Big numbers trip people up because of the zeros, not the maths. This one trick makes them much easier to handle out loud.
body:
The problem

4.5 million customers × $300 a year. Revenue?

Step by step

  1. 4.5 M = 4.5 × 10⁶ 300 = 3 × 10²
  2. 4.5 × 3 = 13.5
  3. 10⁶ × 10² = 10⁸

Answer: $1.35 billion.

How to say it in the interview

Four and a half million customers, each paying three hundred dollars a year. What is the revenue?

Split each number into a small number and its zeros.

Multiply the small numbers: four and a half times three is thirteen and a half.

Then add the zeros: six plus two is eight.

So the answer is thirteen and a half times ten to the eight: one point three five billion dollars.

Say the method out loud as you go, so the interviewer can follow, and catch you before a slip.

Notice that the last step is always about meaning. A number on its own earns half the marks; a number with "so what" earns all of them.
outro: Practise sums like this in the free case maths drill. Next in this topic: How do you work out percentages in your head quickly?
